namespace.label: Namespace
namespace.definition: A named domain within which identifiers or definitions have a specific, governed meaning. The namespace may appear as an identifier prefix, such as FED in FED-001, or as the name of a containing registry section or controlled vocabulary.

artifact.label: Artifact
artifact.definition: Any identifiable item or body of material created, maintained, used, generated, or preserved by the project. Artifacts include components as well as fragments, intermediate outputs, temporary materials, and other items that do not constitute whole project units.

component.label: Component
component.definition: An artifact that constitutes a whole, distinct unit representing a form, function, product, or other identifiable element of the project.

registry.label: Registry
registry.definition:
A governed, structured catalog of components that records their identifiers, definitions, attributes, relationships, and status within one or more namespaces.

A registry may reference supporting artifacts, but its registered entries are components.

component_class.label: Component class
component_class.definition: A governed category describing what kind of whole unit a component is, based on its fundamental form or function. The Stage 2 classes are document, configuration, dataset, script, log, agent, bot, and interface. An inventory item that cannot be classified coherently within this set creates a design stop; it does not authorize an implementation-time extension.

configuration.label: Configuration
configuration.definition: A component that establishes structured values, definitions, mappings, or operating parameters used by another component or project process.

dataset.label: Dataset
dataset.definition: A component consisting of a maintained, structured collection of related data that is governed and used as a whole unit. A generated data file subordinate to another component remains a supporting artifact unless it has independent identity, maintenance, or governed treatment.

script.label: Script
script.definition: An executable source component that performs a defined computational or automation function.

log.label: Log
log.definition: A component that preserves an ordered collection of entries documenting states, events, transitions, observations, or work over time. A valid log may presently contain a single entry, but the component's organizing form remains an ordered entry collection rather than a current-state handoff or ordinary document.

agent.label: Agent
agent.definition: An executable component capable of applying reasoning or adaptive judgment to perform work within a governed scope.

bot.label: Bot
bot.definition: An executable component that performs a repeatable, bounded class of work under defined configuration and authority.

interface.label: Interface
interface.definition: A component through which a human, machine, or both interact with project information or functionality.

lifecycle_model.label: Lifecycle model
lifecycle_model.definition: The governed progression of lifecycle states applicable to a component.

lifecycle_state.label: Lifecycle state
lifecycle_state.definition: A standardized, named position within that progression describing a component's current relationship to the project.

canonical_source.label: Canonical source
canonical_source.definition:
The component designated as the controlling source for a defined body of content, data, configuration, rules, or functionality.

Other components may derive from, render, copy, or use it, but they do not replace its controlling role unless that role is formally reassigned.

generated_output.label: Generated output
generated_output.definition: An artifact produced by a defined process from one or more source components, artifacts, or governed inputs. A generated output may be a partial artifact or a whole component, and it is maintained by reproducing its generating process rather than by independently editing the output.

temporary_artifact.label: Temporary artifact
temporary_artifact.definition:
An artifact created or retained for a bounded, temporary purpose during a process and not intended to remain a canonical or durable project unit after that purpose is fulfilled.

An artifact is temporary because of its governed purpose and disposition—not merely because of its name, path, or apparent age.

cache.label: Cache
cache.definition: An artifact or component that stores a replaceable copy, derived result, or reusable material to improve access or execution efficiency. A cache is not the canonical source of what it contains and may be refreshed or regenerated from its governing source or process.

component_relationship.label: Component relationship
component_relationship.definition: A governed connection between two or more components that identifies how they interact or relate, such as dependency, implementation, validation, verification, consumption, or succession.

dependency.label: Dependency
dependency.definition: A component relationship in which one component requires another component for its intended function, valid interpretation, or governed operation. Without the required component, the dependent component cannot be treated as complete or operating as intended.

producer.label: Producer
producer.definition:
The person, process, tool, or component responsible for creating or updating an artifact or component through a defined method.

A producer identifies how an item comes into being or is maintained; it does not by itself determine the item's authority or ownership.

component_owner.label: Component owner
component_owner.definition:
The person or governed role accountable for a component's stewardship, including its maintenance, review, and lifecycle disposition.

Ownership does not necessarily mean that the owner created the component, produces its outputs, or may change it without required approval.

authority_model.label: Authority model
authority_model.definition:
A governed assignment of control over decisions, rules, content, state, or actions within a defined scope, including who or what may establish, approve, or change them.

Authority is scope-specific. Ownership, production, possession, or technical ability does not by itself create authority.

validation.label: Validation
validation.definition:
A governed process for determining whether an artifact or component satisfies defined requirements using specified evidence or methods.

A successful validation establishes conformity with those requirements; it does not by itself confer approval, authority, adoption, or activation.

validator.label: Validator
validator.definition:
The person, process, tool, or component responsible for checking whether an artifact or component conforms to defined requirements using specified evidence or methods.

A validator applies the requirements; it does not define, waive, or change them unless separately assigned that authority.

approval.label: Approval
approval.definition:
A recorded decision by an authorized person or process accepting an artifact, component, change, or action for a defined purpose or stage.

Approval is limited to its stated scope. It does not imply activation, publication, execution, or broader authority unless those outcomes are expressly included.

adoption.label: Adoption
adoption.definition:
A logged, authorized act that incorporates an artifact, component, definition, rule, or change into the project's current governed state.

Adoption makes the adopted item part of the project's governing structure, but it does not necessarily activate execution or authorize publication unless separately stated.

activation.label: Activation
activation.definition: A logged, authorized act that places a component into governed operational use for a defined scope.

active_operational_status.label: Active
active_operational_status.definition: Authorized and enabled to execute within a defined operational scope. An active executable component may currently be idle.

paused_operational_status.label: Paused
paused_operational_status.definition: Temporarily prevented from executing while retained for possible resumption.

inactive_operational_status.label: Inactive
inactive_operational_status.definition: Not enabled to execute within the applicable operational scope.

current_applicability_status.label: Current
current_applicability_status.definition: Designated as the presently governing or applicable version of a component. A component can be active without being current.

draft_lifecycle_state.label: Draft
draft_lifecycle_state.definition: Under development and not yet submitted for possible adoption.

proposed_lifecycle_state.label: Proposed
proposed_lifecycle_state.definition: Submitted for possible adoption but not yet incorporated into the project’s governed state.

adopted_lifecycle_state.label: Adopted
adopted_lifecycle_state.definition: Incorporated into the project's governed state through an authorized adoption.

retired_lifecycle_state.label: Retired
retired_lifecycle_state.definition: No longer designated for current use in its former role. Retirement does not determine whether the component is retained or archived.

archived_retention_posture.label: Archived
archived_retention_posture.definition: Retained for historical, evidentiary, or provenance purposes rather than current operational use. Archived is a retention posture, not a lifecycle state.

supersession_relationship.label: Supersession
supersession_relationship.definition: The governed replacement of one component by another in a defined role, function, or authority.

predecessor_relationship_role.label: Predecessor
predecessor_relationship_role.definition: The earlier component in a succession relationship.

successor_relationship_role.label: Successor
successor_relationship_role.definition: The component that follows or replaces a predecessor in a defined role, function, or authority.

alias_identifier_relationship.label: Alias
alias_identifier_relationship.definition: An alternate identifier or locator that refers to the same component without creating a separate component.

identifier.label: Identifier
identifier.definition: A name or code that distinguishes an artifact or component within a namespace.

stable_identifier.label: Stable identifier
stable_identifier.definition: An identifier intended to remain unchanged when a component’s name, location, revision, or status changes.

locator.label: Locator
locator.definition: A value indicating where an artifact or component can be found or accessed. A locator may change without changing the component’s identity.

revision.label: Revision
revision.definition: A particular changed state in the continuing history of the same artifact or component.

version.label: Version
version.definition: A formally designated edition of an artifact or component, which may encompass one or more revisions.

attribute.label: Attribute
attribute.definition: A governed property recorded about an artifact or component, such as its class, owner, status, or disclosure posture.

classification.label: Classification
classification.definition: The governed assignment of an artifact or component to one or more defined categories based on specified characteristics.

disposition.label: Disposition
disposition.definition: A governed determination of how an artifact or component will be retained, transferred, superseded, archived, or otherwise handled.

migration.label: Migration
migration.definition: A governed change in a component’s location, structure, identifier, or technical form that preserves defined continuity with its prior state.

redirect.label: Redirect
redirect.definition: A mechanism that directs use of an earlier identifier or locator to a designated current identifier or locator.

provenance.label: Provenance
provenance.definition: The documented origin and complete governed history of an artifact or component, including every logged change to its identity, content, location, form, status, relationships, authority, ownership, or disposition. This includes revision, derivation, migration, adoption, activation, supersession, retirement, and archival.

derivation.label: Derivation
derivation.definition:
A relationship in which an artifact or component is produced from one or more sources through copying, extraction, transformation, calculation, generation, or synthesis.

Synthesis is a specific type of derivation: synthesis combines multiple sources into a new coherent whole, whereas other derivations may be copies, extracts, renders, hashes, conversions, or generated reports.

source.label: Source
source.definition: An artifact, component, or governed input from which material is obtained, produced, or evaluated. A source is not necessarily the canonical source.

source_binding.label: Source binding
source_binding.definition: A recorded connection between an artifact or component and the exact source content or revision upon which it depends.

evidence.label: Evidence
evidence.definition: Information or material used to support a determination, decision, validation, or verification.

receipt.label: Receipt
receipt.definition: A logged artifact documenting that a defined action or transaction occurred and recording the evidence needed to verify it.

governing.label: Governing
governing.definition: Assigned to establish or control requirements, meaning, behavior, or decisions within a defined scope.

authoritative.label: Authoritative
authoritative.definition: Possessing governed control over a defined decision, rule, content, state, or action within a specified scope.

nonauthoritative.label: Nonauthoritative
nonauthoritative.definition: Informational or supporting in purpose and not permitted to establish or control the matter it describes.

verification.label: Verification
verification.definition: A process for confirming a specific claim, fact, identity, or result through direct comparison with defined evidence. Unlike validation, verification confirms what is true or occurred; validation determines whether requirements are satisfied.

document.label: Document
document.definition: A whole artifact organized to communicate, preserve, or govern information in a readable form.

specification.label: Specification
specification.definition: A document that defines the required characteristics, structure, behavior, or interfaces of a particular component, product, system, or output, including the requirements by which conformity can be validated by human or automated processes.

governing_document.label: Governing document
governing_document.definition: A document assigned authority to establish requirements, definitions, decisions, or procedures within a defined scope.

schema.label: Schema
schema.definition: A component that formally defines the permitted structure, fields, values, and constraints of a class of structured artifacts.

implementation.label: Implementation
implementation.definition: A component that technically realizes a defined function, process, interface, rule, or specification.

test_suite.label: Test suite
test_suite.definition: A script type containing a maintained collection of executable checks used to verify or validate defined behavior or requirements. A test suite defines the checks; an individual execution result, report, or log is a separate artifact.

consumer.label: Consumer
consumer.definition: A person, process, tool, or component that uses an artifact, component, service, or output for a defined purpose.

consumption.label: Consumption
consumption.definition:
A relationship in which one component uses another component or its output without assuming ownership or authority over it.

These dimensions are not mutually exclusive. A component may concurrently be retired, archived, a predecessor, and superseded by another component; its successor may concurrently be current and, when executable, active.

allow_children.label: Allow children
allow_children.definition: A directory-scope control indicating that ordinary descendant paths may inherit the scope's placement governance without individual registration, subject to more-specific scopes and explicit treatments.

ordinary_scoped_child.label: Ordinary scoped child
ordinary_scoped_child.definition: A persistent artifact whose placement is governed by a recursive directory scope and which is not independently registered, assigned as a supporting artifact, or covered by a component-registration exemption.

component_registration_exemption.label: Component registration exemption
component_registration_exemption.definition: A governed categorical rule that relieves covered artifacts from individual component registration while leaving placement, producer, information handling, retention, disposition, and coverage controls in force.

unresolved.label: Unresolved
unresolved.definition: A coverage result for an in-scope path with no valid treatment or with conflicting or multiple treatments, requiring human review before validation may pass.

revision_mode.label: Revision mode
revision_mode.definition: A governed property specifying how revisions to a retained component or artifact may be made.

append_only_revision_mode.label: Append-only
append_only_revision_mode.definition: New entries are permitted while existing entries remain unchanged.

immutable_revision_mode.label: Immutable
immutable_revision_mode.definition: The item is not altered; a correction requires a new or superseding component or record.

replaceable_revision_mode.label: Replaceable
replaceable_revision_mode.definition: The item may be regenerated or replaced from its governing source.

design_contract.label: Design contract
design_contract.definition: An exact owner-submitted implementation authority that permits a defined implementing process to make only the changes within its fixed scope, invariants, stop conditions, and mutation authorities.

owner_direct.label: Owner direct
owner_direct.definition: An exact authenticated instruction directly from Benjamin authorizing an identified action within a fixed scope. This evidence mode remains unavailable to production validation until a separately approved trusted resolver exists.

execution_controls.label: Execution controls
execution_controls.definition: Governed restrictions specifying who or what may initiate an executable component and for which purposes.

automated_initiation.label: Automated initiation
automated_initiation.definition: Execution initiated by an authorized coordinator within a governed chain and only when its defined due condition is satisfied.

manual_initiation.label: Manual initiation
manual_initiation.definition: Execution initiated only after an explicit current human instruction.

llm_assisted.label: LLM-assisted
llm_assisted.definition: A manual execution interface in which a language-model-assisted process carries out an explicit current human instruction without originating execution authority.

direct_script.label: Direct script
direct_script.definition: A manual execution interface in which a human directly invokes the governed script under an explicit current instruction.

explicit_current_human_instruction.label: Explicit current human instruction
explicit_current_human_instruction.definition: A present, unambiguous human instruction authorizing the specific execution; an earlier or unrelated approval is insufficient.

due_under_governed_cadence.label: Due under governed cadence
due_under_governed_cadence.definition: The executable stage is due under its separately governed runtime cadence and coordinator decision.
